title: Protocol for the Generation of Definitive Hematopoietic Progenitors from Human Pluripotent Stem Cells
protocol: Deplete feeder cells from hPSC cultures.
Incubate the depleted cultures for at least 2 hours.
Reduce the concentration of mouse feeder cells in hPSC cultures before starting the differentiation protocol.
Passage hPSCs onto feeder medium-coated flasks at least 2 hours before the differentiation start point.
Harvest hPSCs using TrypLETM Select for hESCs or EDTA based dissociation medium for hiPSCs.
Add sufficient volume of reagent to cover the flask surface (0.5 mL per T25 flask, 1.5 mL per T75 flask).
Remove feeder medium from the pre-coated T75 flask.
Rinse the flask with PBS.
Add 15 mL of hESC or hiPSC media to the flask.
Pellet the cells and re-plate at a 1:1 ratio.
Incubate in low O2 conditions.
Allow at least 2 hours for the cells to reattach.
Use cells from a confluent T75 flask to set up ten 96-well plates.
Place 60 EBs per plate, corresponding to approximately 5,000–6,000 input cells per well.
Generate EBs using a spin-based method by aggregating undifferentiated hPSCs through centrifugation onto round-bottom, low attachment 96-well plates.
Single-cell dissociate hPSCs and plate in non-adherent round-bottom 96-well plates.
Aggregate hPSCs by centrifugation, yielding 60 EBs/plate.
Culture EBs in Stage 1 medium for 4 days.
Treat EBs with Activin inhibitor (SB) and WNT-agonist (CHIR) at day 1.7 to pattern mesoderm toward intra-embryonic hematopoietic program.
Remove medium containing SB/CHIR using a multichannel pipette, angled to avoid disturbing the non-adherent EBs.
Culture EBs in Stage 2 growth factors that promote endothelial development until day 8.
Transfer EB cultures to adherent wells in Stage 3 media on day 8 to allow outgrowth of stromal and endothelial cells.
Perform half medium changes from day 14 by tilting the pipette to avoid removal of blood progenitors in suspension.
Add 70 μL sterile distilled water to the outer 30 wells of ten 96-well plates.
Prepare 50 mL Stage 1 differentiation media with BVSAF cytokines.
Harvest cells from a T75 flask (95%–100% confluent) using Accutase® solution by incubating for 3 minutes at 37°C.
Rinse out the tube with differentiation medium to collect all the cells.
Mix gently and transfer the cell pellet into the 50 mL Stage 1 differentiation media.
Transfer the cell-medium mixture, aliquoting 80 μL per well, using only the inner 60 wells of the ten low attachment 96-well plates previously prepared.
Aggregate the cells at the bottom of each well by centrifuging for 2 minutes at 4°C at 400 × g.
Place the plates into a 5% CO2 incubator under normoxic conditions at 37°C.
Evaluate EB formation under the microscope on day 1 of differentiation.
Prepare a mixture of STAPEL medium with added SB and CHIR to make final concentrations per well: SB431542 at 3.5 μM and CHIR99021 at 3 μM.
Place this mixture in a sterile reagent reservoir.
Using a multichannel pipette, add 20 μL of the STAPEL + SB/CHIR mixture into each well of the spin-EBs plates.
Ensure the final volume in each well is 100 μL.
Place the plates back into the incubator.
Add the STAPEL + SB/CHIR mixture approximately 42 hours after the onset of differentiation.
Remove SB/CHIR from EB plates at day 4 of differentiation.
Replace removed inhibitors with media containing a mix of growth factors to support hematopoietic mesoderm development to endothelium.
Check under the microscope that EBs appear round with defined sharp edges.
Prepare Stage 2 differentiation mixture using STAPEL media with BVSIF cytokines.
Remove approximately 70–80 μL of Stage 1 medium from each well without disturbing EBs.
Place removed medium in a sterile reservoir to retrieve any fallen EBs.
Check for missing EBs by holding plates against the light.
Add 100 μL of Stage 2 differentiation mixture per well using a multichannel pipette.
Return plates to the incubator and leave until day 7 of differentiation.
Conduct flow cytometric analysis on day 7 to evaluate mesoderm patterning and differentiation kinetics.
Check under the microscope that EBs display a sharp edge without notable cell growth around them.
Collect 10–20 EBs in a tube and let them settle by gravity for approximately 2 minutes, or alternatively pellet the EBs by centrifugation at 400 × g for 2 minutes.
Carefully remove the supernatant and incubate the EBs in 1 mL TrypLETM Select for 30 minutes in a water bath at 37°C.
Dissociate the EBs by passing them through a 23G needle 10 times, or until no clumps remain in the suspension.
Filter the cell suspensions through a 50 μm strainer filter into a 5-mL round-bottom tube used for flow cytometry.
Wash the cells with FACS buffer (phosphate buffered saline (PBS) with 2% FBS) and pellet by centrifugation.
Remove the supernatant from the cell pellet.
Resuspend the cell pellet in 60 μL of FACS buffer.
Transfer 10 μL into a fresh tube as an unstained or isotype control.
Stain 50 μL with CD90-APC (dilution 1:100).
Stain 50 μL with CD34-PeCy7 (dilution 1:100).
Stain 50 μL with CD43-BV (dilution 1:50).
Incubate the stained cells for 15 min at 4°C in a covered ice bucket or in the fridge.
Wash the tubes twice by adding 2 mL of FACS buffer and pelleting by centrifugation.
Resuspend the washed cells in 300 μL PBS prior to analysis in the flow cytometer.
Coat tissue culture treated 6-well plates with 2 mL of Matrigel Solution.
Place the coated plates into a 5% CO2 incubator under normoxic conditions at 37°C overnight (12–18 h) or for a minimum of 60 min.
Transfer EBs from 96-well plates into Matrigel pre-coated plates using a multichannel pipette.
Aspirate the Matrigel solution from all wells.
Set the multichannel pipette at 100 μL and use only four pipette tips per well of a 6-well plate.
Transfer 20-30 EBs per well, depending on harvest time for analysis.
Place plates in the incubator to allow EBs to attach overnight (12-18 h).
Do not move the plates during the first 24 hours.
Check EBs under brightfield microscopy on day 9 for successful attachment and commencing growth of adherent endothelial and stromal cells around the EBs.
Gently remove the medium without disturbing the EBs on day 9.
Add 2 ml of Stage 3 medium to each well for 6-well plates or 10 ml for 10-cm plates, being careful not to direct the medium stream onto the EBs.
Top up wells with 1 ml of Stage 3 medium at day 11 for 6-well plates or 3–5 ml for 10-cm plates.
Aspirate Stage 3 medium from the wells.
Add 2 mL per well of Stage 3 Specific medium.
Place plates back into the incubator.
Top up the wells with 2–3 mL of fresh Stage 3 Specific medium two days after initial setup.
Perform half medium changes every 2 days thereafter.
Carefully remove 2 mL from the surface of the medium by tilting the plates and aspirating from the edge.
Add 2 mL of fresh medium slowly without disturbing the cultures.
For 10-cm plates, top up with 5 mL of fresh medium every 3–4 days.
If concerned about losing hematopoietic cells during medium changes, transfer 2 mL of culture medium to a 10 mL conical polystyrene tube.
Centrifuge the transferred medium at 400 × g for 3 minutes.
Discard the supernatant and resuspend the pelleted hematopoietic cells with 2 mL of fresh medium.
Re-add the resuspended cells to the culture well.
Harvest cell fractions for subsequent analysis of adherent hematopoietic cultures.
Consider the specific cell fraction(s) of interest for experimental design and analyses.
Collect CD34+ blood progenitors in suspension from cultures.
Isolate progenitor cells attached to the endothelium or trapped within EBs.
Harvest progenitors immediately after the endothelial to hematopoietic transition, generally from days 13–15 of differentiation.
Detach adherent progenitors and collect them from the medium starting around day 16 of differentiation.
Collect the highest number of hematopoietic progenitors in suspension usually coinciding with days 18–22 of differentiation.
Perform cell sorting immediately after harvesting to enrich for specific or more immature cell fractions.
Collect supernatants containing “floating” blood cells in a 50 mL tube and place them on ice.
Rinse the wells gently with 1 mL PBS to collect remaining suspension and loosely attached blood cells.
Combine the collected suspension into the main tube.
Pellet the cells by centrifugation at 4°C.
Keep tubes on ice until other cell fractions are harvested or use directly for downstream analyses.
Add 500 μL of TrypLETM and incubate at 37°C for 5 minutes to detach EBs.
Transfer the EBs into a sterile tube containing 1 mL of 2 mg/mL collagenase Type 4 diluted in IMDM.
Incubate for 30–45 minutes in a 37°C water bath.
Detach remaining stromal-endothelial layer by pipetting up and down or using a cell scraper.
Pellet cells by centrifugation and keep on ice.
Dissociate EBs by passing the suspension through increasing needle gauges from 18G to 25G.
Pellet the cells to remove residual collagenase reagent.
Resuspend the cells in PBS.
Filter the cell suspensions through a 70 μm sterile strainer cap sitting on a 50 mL tube.
Rinse any remaining cells with PBS and pass through the 70 μm filter.
Pellet the filtered suspension for subsequent analysis.
Analyze the pellet using clonogenic assays or flow cytometry based on hematopoietic cell surface markers.
